Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?
questions.worked_solution:
We notice the following:

- The horizontal component (i.e., the $i$ component) is negative for each vector in our vector field. Therefore, we can rule out the following options:

$$
F(x,y)=i-2\,j,\,H(x,y)=i
$$

- The vertical component (i.e., the $j$ component) is positive for each vector in our vector field. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
K(x,y)=-j
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram corresponds to the vector field $G(x,y)=-i+j.$

Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?

We notice the following:

- The vertical component (i.e., the $j$ component) is zero for *every* vector in our vector field. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
H(x,y)=y\,i+j
$$

- As we move away from the origin in the vertical direction, our vectors' horizontal components (i.e., the $i$ components) get longer. Therefore, we can rule out the following options:

$$
F(x,y)=x\,i,\,K(x,y)=-i
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram corresponds to the vector field $G(x,y)=y\,i.$

Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?
questions.worked_solution:
We notice the following:

- Each vector in our vector field is parallel to the $x$-axis. So, the $j$ and $k$ components of our vector field are zero everywhere. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
F(x,y,z)=i+x\,j
$$

- Moreover, each vector in our vector field is pointing in the *positive* $x$-direction, so the $i$ component of our vector field is positive. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
G(x,y,z)=-i
$$

- Finally, we note that each vector in our vector field has the same length, so the $i$ component of our vector field is constant. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
H(x,y,z)=x\,i
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram corresponds to the vector field $K(x,y,z)=2\,i.$

- Finally, we note that each vector in our vector field has the same length, so the $k$ component of our vector field is constant. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:
